S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.

subtypes.Intrusive Memories: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Distressing Dreams: Recurrent distressing dreams in which the content and/or affect of the dream are related to the traumatic event.
subtypes.Dissociative Reactions (Flashbacks): Dissociative reactions (e.g., flashbacks) in which the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring.
subtypes.Psychological Distress at Cues: Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Physiological Reactions to Cues: Marked physiological reactions to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.

subtypes.Internal Avoidance: Efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings about or closely associated with the traumatic event.
subtypes.External Avoidance: Efforts to avoid external reminders (people, places, conversations, activities, objects, situations) that arouse distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).

subtypes.Fragmented Memory: Inability to recall only specific parts of the traumatic event while remembering others.
subtypes.Generalized Amnesia: Inability to recall the majority or the entirety of the traumatic event.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.

subtypes.Impulsive Anger: Sudden explosions of anger for trivial reasons or no clear reason.
subtypes.Verbal Aggression: Attacking others with shouting, cursing, or blame without holding back.
subtypes.Physical Aggression: Physically attacking people or throwing/breaking objects.
subtypes.Chronic Irritability: A state where nerves are always sharp and sensitive, ready to explode at the slightest touch.

S080.name: Exaggerated_Startle_Response
S080.description: Exaggerated startle response to minor stimuli.

subtypes.Auditory Startle: Startling excessively and flinching physically at sudden noises.
subtypes.Tactile Startle: Being extremely startled by unexpected physical contact.
subtypes.Visual Startle: Being greatly startled and wary of sudden appearances of people or rapid movements.
subtypes.Slow Recovery: Heart pounding and trembling for a long time after being startled, not calming down easily.

patient_info.stressor_event: Detention in jail or other institution
patient_info.stressor: Lorenzo was detained overnight after a mistaken identification during a late courier run, and while in a crowded holding area he witnessed a violent assault at close range before officers rushed everyone against the wall. Over the next week, he could not return to night deliveries, avoided the route near the detention facility, and had intrusive flashes of the holding cell while being unable to piece together the minutes when the fight first broke out. His sleep deteriorated, he startled at radios, sirens, and slammed doors, and his anger flared at dispatch and at a pickup basketball game, leaving him unable to work safely or keep his volunteer commitments. After he missed two shifts and arrived visibly shaken at his men’s stress-support group, the group facilitator helped him arrange same-day psychiatric assessment.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: I barely sleep now—I'll doze off for an hour or two, then I'm up from some dream about that cell or a door slamming, and by morning I feel too wrecked to drive my route.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
S069.manifestation: What brings me in is these flashes keep hitting me out of nowhere, like I'm back in that crowded holding room seeing the fight and hearing everybody get shoved to the wall, even when I'm just standing at a pickup counter.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.
S070.manifestation: I've been turning down night runs and taking the long way around town because I can't make myself go near that detention building or talk about what happened without feeling like I'm right back there.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).
S071.manifestation: I remember pieces, like the guy on the floor and the officers yelling, but the part where the fight first started is missing, like my mind skips over those minutes no matter how hard I try.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.
S077.manifestation: My temper has been snapping for no reason, like I blew up at dispatch over a schedule change and then cursed out a guy at basketball for bumping me when normally I'd just shake it off.

S080.name: Exaggerated_Startle_Response
S080.description: Exaggerated startle response to minor stimuli.
S080.manifestation: Every radio crackle, siren, or slammed door makes me jump like I'm about to get rushed, and my heart keeps pounding so hard afterward that I have to pull over or step outside.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I’ve already missed two shifts, and when I try to work I don’t feel safe driving or handling deliveries because I’m too shaken and on edge. I also stopped showing up for my volunteer commitments because I can’t keep it together around people right now.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about a week, ever since I was detained overnight and saw that assault in the holding area.
